course_name_original: Dispositivos y Circuitos Electrónicos de Potencia
prerequisites: The students must certify that they have passed basic skills and competences in electronics devices and circuits. This can be accomplished at his/her incoming student profile and CV.

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modelling and simulation of power systems.
Critical analysis of the information coming from the sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Asses the risks of the use of electrical energy, as well as those of industrial installations, understanding the necessity of safety elements, protections and signalling in power systems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems.
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical.
Ability to plan and organize work.
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity.
Concern for quality and achievement motivation.
Characterization and modelling of the main energy sources and electric power loads.
Characterization, operation and design of electronic topologies and control methods for electric energy conversion.
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems.
Acquire the basic knowledge of power electronics to analyse and design electrical power systems.
Acquire the knowledge of power electronics needed to analyse and design electrical and hybrid traction systems.
Understanding the basic principles of power electronics conversion, as well as the operating principle of the main power devices (semiconductor, passive, control, etc.).
Manage specific software simulation and modeling of devices and electronic circuits and specific laboratory equipment.
Select electronic components and basic configuration most appropriate given operating conditions required.

Select, model and analyze the operation of most power electronic devices used depending on specific applications, taking into account also all the auxiliary equipment required for this operation (drivers, snubbers, etc.).
Application of the most appropriate techniques for power electronic conversion, basic configurations and switching elements, conversion and control.
Integrate knowledge previously viewed by selecting the appropriate topology and components with a given power application.
Manage specific software simulation of electronic circuits and specific laboratory equipment.
Basic modelling of power loads and power supplies to carry out simulations of a full power electronics system.

syllabus_topics: Review of the physical principles of operation of semiconductor devices:

Basic concepts about semiconductor materials: band diagrams, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, mechanisms for electric current conduction and continuity equation and its use in simple steady-state and transient situations.
Basic concepts about PN junctions: Equilibrium conditions, forward- and reverse-biased operation and calculation of the current flow when biased.
Reverse-biased voltage limits of PN junctions.
Transient effects in PN junctions in switching-mode operation.
Thermal management in power semiconductor devices:
Equivalent electric circuits for thermal phenomena.
Introduction to the transient thermal models.
Drivers for source-grounded and source-floating power MOSFETs.
Equivalent circuits based on BJTs and MOSFETs.
Parasitic active devices inside a IGBT.
The SCR: internal structure and equivalent circuit based on BJTs.
Static and dynamic characteristics of SCRs.
topologies in terms of number of switches
topologies with and without galvanic isolation

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests. short answer tests and / or test development)

assessment_rules: The assessment is divided into two parts: Power Electronic Devices (PED) and Power Electronic Circuits (PEC). Each written exam (PED 30%, PEC 20%) requires a minimum score of 4/10 to pass. Similarly, each assignment/project (PED 25%, PEC 15%), consisting of a report and a 15-minute presentation, also requires a minimum score of 4/10 to pass. Activities (PED 5%, PEC 5%) involve individual assignments throughout the semester. For differentiated assessment, students must attend the exam and deliver projects by the due date, with project presentations agreed upon with the lecturer, potentially via teleconference.
